maria_support: Hey team — customer on prod (tenant: tenant-84) reporting repeated MFA prompts after they changed their AD password this morning. They can authenticate via SSO initially but after the first redirect they immediately get kicked back to login and a fresh MFA challenge.

maria_support: Repro steps from customer: 1) Login via SSO > 2) Accept device trust prompt > 3) SSO returns to /auth/callback with code > 4) Redirect to app, immediately asks to re-enter credentials + MFA. They said it started after a password rotation.

maria_support: Quick check: session cookie present in browser (`.rdw_session`) but looks like it's a new Set-Cookie on every redirect. Customer sent screenshots showing two different `sid` values in consecutive requests.

jordan_sre: Noted. Can you grab the auth logs and the session cookie headers? Also need the `x-redwood-tenant` header from the failing requests. Might be a stale refresh token/refresh-token rotation mismatch.

maria_support: Pasted redacted headers the customer gave: ```
GET /auth/callback?code=abc123  Host: app.customer.example  Cookie: .rdw_session=eyJhbGci...; SameSite=None; Secure  x-redwood-tenant: tenant-84  User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0...
Set-Cookie: .rdw_session=eyJhbGci...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None; Max-Age=1200
```

maria_support: They also included this log from their browser console: `AuthError: refresh_token_invalid - refresh token mismatch`

samir_eng: That error smells like refresh-token rotation is enabled but our session store still holds the old refresh token for the user. After AD password change the IdP might be invalidating tokens and issuing new ones — if our refresh-token check compares against a stored fingerprint we could be rejecting the new one and forcing reauth loops.

samir_eng: Can you capture the sequence of redirects server-side? We need the raw responses from our `/oauth/complete` handler. If the server issues a new session cookie before exchanging the code for tokens, that could create a race.

maria_support: I asked the customer for HAR file and the raw response bodies. They uploaded a truncated HAR — attached a snippet showing two Set-Cookie responses from our domain within 1s.

jordan_sre: If two Set-Cookie calls happen, likely we have both a fallback cookie issued by the auth service and then the backend replacing it. That makes the browser send the second cookie (new sid) while the backend is validating against the first token. We should check the order and whether SameSite or Path differ. Also check `HttpOnly`/`Secure` — customer is on HTTPS so should be fine.

eva_security: Adding context from security: we recently rolled out a change to device-trust revalidation for AD users — when password change detected at IdP, we mark device trust stale and force MFA re-enroll. If the IdP is simultaneously revoking refresh tokens, that could create a timing window where the token we get at callback is no longer valid by the time our session store writes. We need correlation ids: do we have `x-request-id` in the failures?

maria_support: Customer logged `x-request-id: req-7f9a2c` and included server logs showing: `WARN oauth: refresh token validation failed for user u-123 (token mismatch) req-7f9a2c` right after `INFO oauth: created new session sid=s-999 for callback req-7f9a2c`. So order is create session -> validate token -> fail -> prompt reauth.

samir_eng: Ok that's actionable. Looks like we create the session before we've fully validated the token set. Two potential fixes: 1) delay setting persistent session cookie until token validation and device-trust checks complete; or 2) if we must set early, include a short-lived handshake cookie to tie the subsequent token validation to the same SID. The first is cleaner.

jordan_sre: For the customer right now, we can ask them to clear cookies and do a fresh login; but that won't fix root cause. For a temporary server-side mitigation: we can patch to drop the pre-validation Set-Cookie. I'll open an emergency PR to gate the cookie write behind token validation.

maria_support: I'll tell the customer the temporary workaround (clear cookies + re-login) and that engineering is looking into a fix. They asked for repro timeline and will await an update.

session-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-8842 | Priority: P2 | Owner: samir_eng | Link: https://redwood.internal/inc/INC-2026-8842

samir_eng: Opening a draft branch now. Patch plan: change oauth/complete flow to validate `id_token` and `refresh_token` before calling `sessionStore.create(session)`; add unit tests simulating IdP revoke between code exchange and session write; add an integration test with a mocked IdP that rotates refresh tokens on password change.

eva_security: Also add detection and alerting for repeated Set-Cookie patterns on `/auth/callback` (>=2 within 2s) so SRE can triage faster. Could be a nice signal in Console.

jordan_sre: Will add a tracing span and a log metric for double-set-cookie events. Also check existing canaries to see if any customers showed this after our device-trust rollout last week.

maria_support: Customer is ok with the P2 and wants ETA for a fix. Samir, can you share an estimate?

samir_eng: I can have a hotfix PR by EOD and a canary deploy to staging tomorrow morning. If staging looks good, we can roll to prod with a 10% canary and monitor for regressions. ETA end of day for PR, 24-36h for full prod rollout assuming no surprises.

maria_support: Thanks — I'll update the ticket and ping the customer. Adding follow-up: request HAR + cookie dump if this happens again.

maria_support: Quick note for support runbook: when customer reports immediate MFA loop after password rotation, ask for HAR, `x-request-id`, `x-redwood-tenant`, and whether device trust prompt was accepted. Suggest immediate cookie clear to break loop.

eva_security: We'll also review the device-trust change and consider adding a short grace window for token rotation during password changes to reduce UX loops.

jordan_sre: Cool. Marking thread resolved for now, please reopen if customer sees it again after the hotfix. :white_check_mark:
